claims.text: Successful formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by a narrow kinetic window.
Nearly simultaneous reduction of all metal precursors ensures uniform atomic incorporation.
Uniform atomic incorporation suppresses phase separation and elemental segregation.
Coordinating agents prevent premature aggregation of the precursors or nascent particles.
A precisely controlled rapid energetic input can synchronize reduction kinetics across the constituent metal species.
Additional ligands can produce differential reduction behavior among the metal precursors.
Rapid reduction produces transient, uniformly nucleated metal clusters.
Uniformly nucleated clusters act as seeds for concurrent alloying.
Local d-band filling and environmental electronegativity are related electronic properties in noble-metal high-entropy alloys.
Aligning precursor reduction rates causes d-band filling and electronegativity effects to interact in a balanced way.
Synchronized reduction minimizes differential nucleation and growth.
Minimizing differential nucleation and growth prevents phase and elemental segregation and produces a single-phase solid solution.
Rapid energetic processing will yield nanoparticles with uniform elemental distributions and a single solid-solution phase.
Conventional slower heating will yield mixed-phase particles with noticeable elemental segregation.
Traditional gradual heating often produces heterogeneous or phase-separated structures because precursor reductions are not simultaneous.
The proposed mechanism applies primarily to noble-metal systems whose constituents have relatively similar redox potentials.
Large intrinsic redox-potential differences or strongly differential ligand effects can place a system outside the mechanism's domain.
Minor changes in precursor coordination or solvent interactions may shift the optimal kinetic window.
A controlled comparison of identical precursor mixtures under rapid and gradual heating can test the predicted difference in phase homogeneity and elemental distribution.

If rapid and gradual heating both produce similarly uniform elemental distributions and single-phase solid solutions, the proposed critical role of the narrow kinetic window is falsified for the tested system.

contradictions.description: The initial state includes coordinating agents, while the conditions specify synthesis without additional ligands. It is unclear whether the coordinating agents are intended ligands and, if so, how these requirements can both be satisfied.
